what_its_for: Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate gland, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). It helps relax the muscles in your prostate and bladder neck, making it easier to urinate. Common symptoms it helps with include a weak urine stream, difficulty starting urination, and the need to urinate frequently or urgently.
how_to_take: Take tamsulosin by mouth, exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Take it about 30 minutes after the same meal each day (for example, always after breakfast or always after dinner). This helps the medicine work best and reduces the chance of side effects like dizziness.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 0.4 mg (one capsule) once a day. After 2 to 4 weeks, your doctor may increase your dose to 0.8 mg (two capsules) once a day if your symptoms are not well controlled. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is on the same day you missed it. If you remember the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your regular dose that day. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you miss several days in a row, call your doctor before restarting, as you may need to start back at the lower dose.
storage: Store tamsulosin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires alertness right after you start taking tamsulosin or when your dose is increased, since it can cause dizziness or fainting — especially when standing up quickly. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it can make dizziness worse. Avoid getting up too fast from a sitting or lying position. Tell your eye doctor you take tamsulosin before any eye surgery (such as cataract surgery), as it can affect eye surgery outcomes.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a painful erection that lasts longer than 4 hours (priapism — this is a medical emergency), severe dizziness or fainting, skin rash or itching, swelling of the face or throat, or a sudden decrease or loss of vision. Also contact your doctor if your urinary symptoms do not improve or get worse.
when_it_works: Some men notice improvement in urinary symptoms within a few days to a week, but it may take up to 4 weeks of regular use to feel the full benefit. Keep taking it even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Use with caution if you have significant kidney disease. Older adults: Older men may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure from this medication — take extra care when standing up. Women and children: Tamsulosin is not approved for use in women or children. Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant should avoid handling broken or crushed tamsulosin capsules.
